opportunities.name: GitHub developer lead research and hiring email draft
opportunities.description: Look up the GitHub user {username}, record their follower count, top repo (stars and language) and latest post, then write a lead email to {recipient} for the role {role}.
steps: Open github.com and click the 'Search or jump to' box
Type {username} and press Enter
Click the 'Users' filter in the results sidebar
Open the matching user profile
Note the follower count and open the top pinned repo to note its stars and language
Find the user's latest post (blog or pinned item)
Open the mail compose page
Set To = {recipient}
Set Subject = 'Lead for {role}: {username}'
Set Body = '{username}: {followers} followers, top repo {top_repo} ({stars} stars, {language}), latest post: {latest_post}.'
Send or discard the draft

instances.values: username=karpathy, role=ML Research Engineer, recipient=hiring@example.com; 226k followers, nanoGPT 63.8k stars Python, latest post microgpt
username=gaearon, role=Staff Frontend Engineer, recipient=hiring@example.com; 94k followers, react/react 251k stars JavaScript, latest post 'How I Vibed a Proof of Conway's Conjecture'
username=simonw (Simon Willison); opened the llm repo. No email was seen, so this run looks incomplete

opportunities.name: Person bio plus company homepage snapshot from the Wayback Machine
opportunities.description: Look up {person} on Wikipedia for key facts, check {company_domain} on the Wayback Machine for a snapshot from {year}, and save a combined note.
steps: On Wikipedia, click 'Search Wikipedia', type {person} and press Enter
Note the birth date and current role from the article
Open web.archive.org and type {company_domain} into the URL box, then press Enter
Click {year} on the timeline and open a snapshot date on the calendar
Note the headline on the archived homepage
Open Notes, click 'New note' and type '{person}: {facts}. {company_domain} in {year}: {headline}'
Press Enter to save

instances.values: person=Satya Nadella, company_domain=microsoft.com, year=2014; note: 'Meet the Nokia Lumia 1520 and Lumia 1020'
person=Tim Berners-Lee; the Wayback Machine was opened, but no domain was entered and no note was saved, so this run looks incomplete

opportunities.name: Nearest place walking directions plus neighborhood summary note
opportunities.description: Find the nearest {place_type} to {address} on OpenStreetMap, get walking distance and time, look up {neighborhood} on Wikipedia, and save a note.
steps: On openstreetmap.org, type '{place_type} near {address}' into Search and press Enter
Click the top result
Click 'Find directions between two points' and choose Foot
Set From = {address} and To = the result's name, then press Enter
Note the distance and time
On Wikipedia, search for {neighborhood} and note its one-line description
In Notes, add '{address}: nearest {place_type} {result}, {distance}, {time} walk. {neighborhood}: {description}'

instances.values: address=350 5th Ave, New York, place_type=library, neighborhood=Midtown Manhattan; result 96th Street Library, 5.5 km, 74 min
place_type=coffee, area=Union Square on OSM (no results found); later searched Wikipedia for Chicago Loop. This run looks partial and interleaved with other activity
